title: Apply for an occupation certificate
summary: Learn about the process and requirements for applying for an occupation certificate after completing a development and construction project.
intro:
The last step in the formal development application and construction process is when an occupation certificate is issued.

You need an occupation certificate if you want to:

Occupation certificates are issued by your local council or a private certifier.
who_can_apply: The beneficiary of the development consent
A person with the approval of the beneficiary
A person who is eligible to appoint a principal certifier for the development
what_you_need: A MyServiceNSW Account or your NSW Planning Portal login details
Copies of documents for uploading, such as your fee payment

how_to_steps.text: Select ‘Log in with a Service NSW account’ or enter your NSW Planning Portal login details.
Follow the prompts to complete your application, either:

more_info.text: A partial occupation certificate can be issued for staged building works. A partial occupation certificate allows you to occupy the part of the building that’s been completed.

external_links.text: Submitting an application for an occupation certificate – PDF

faqs.a: Occupation certificates are issued by your local council or a private certifier.

faqs.q: Who can apply for an occupation certificate?
faqs.a: The beneficiary of the development consent, or a person with the approval of the beneficiary, can apply. The application must be made by a person eligible to appoint a principal certifier for the development.

faqs.q: When should I apply for an occupation certificate?
faqs.a: You can apply when you submit your development application (DA) or complying development certificate (CDC), or as a standalone application.
